wikipedia#2.title: 2007: Somali pirates hijacked a North Korean ship in the Indian Ocean northeast of Mogadishu.

wikipedia#3.title: 1999: About 10,000 people died when the most intense tropical cyclone ever recorded in the North Indian Ocean made landfall in the Indian state of Odisha near Bhubaneswar.

wikipedia#4.title: 1998: At 77 years old, former astronaut John Glenn (pictured) returned to space aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery on the STS-95 mission.

wikipedia#5.title: 1991: Galileo became the first spacecraft to visit an asteroid when it made a flyby of Gaspra.

wikipedia#6.title: 1986: British prime minister Margaret Thatcher officially opened the M25, one of Britain's busiest motorways.

wikipedia#7.title: 1960: A C-46 airliner carrying the Cal Poly Mustangs football team crashed during takeoff from Toledo Express Airport in Ohio, U.S., resulting in 22 deaths.

wikipedia#8.title: 1956: The Suez Crisis began with Israel invading the Sinai Peninsula and pushing Egyptian forces back toward the Suez Canal.

wikipedia#9.title: 1956: Suez Crisis: The Israel Border Police massacred 48 Arab citizens in Kafr Qasim, among them women and children who were returning from work.

wikipedia#10.title: 1955: An explosion, likely caused by a World War II–era naval mine, capsized the Soviet ship Novorossiysk in the harbor of Sevastopol, with the loss of 608 men.

wikipedia#11.title: 1948: Arab–Israeli War: The Israel Defense Forces massacred at least 52 villagers while capturing the Palestinian Arab village of Safsaf.

wikipedia#12.title: 1883: The San Francisco Mint signed a contract to produce the Kalākaua coinage (coin pictured) for the Hawaiian Kingdom.

wikipedia#13.title: 1868: The Nanbu clan of Honshu surrendered to Japanese imperial forces during the Boshin War.

wikipedia#14.title: 1863: American Civil War: The Battle of Wauhatchie, one of the few night battles of the war, concluded with the Union Army opening a supply line to troops in Chattanooga, Tennessee.

wikipedia#15.title: 1831: Rioting broke out in Bristol, England, after the Second Reform Bill failed during its passage through Parliament, causing 250 casualties and £300,000 of damage (pictured).

wikipedia#16.title: 1792: William Robert Broughton, a member of George Vancouver's expedition, observed a peak in the present-day U.S. state of Oregon and named it Mount Hood after British admiral Samuel Hood.
